grh_9adb2dd00c0de07e69e9.title: The Shawl
paragraphs: Civil War veteran Arthur Colby dies after spending most of his long life trying to remember a single wondrous event that occurred after he was wounded at Gettysburg. In one final lucid moment he can almost tell Dr. Christian what happened, recalling a hospital, terrible cold and something he must leave behind, but he dies before naming it. Convinced there is a record in Colby's abandoned house, Christian and Judy search it at night. Beneath the bed they find an old trunk containing a shawl, Colby's faded uniform and his wartime diary. The final entries solve the mystery. On July 6, 1863, as the wounded Colby lay outside a hospital shivering while waiting for space inside, a tall man stopped, removed the shawl from his own shoulders, wrapped it around the soldier and spoke kindly to him. The man was Abraham Lincoln. The shawl Colby had struggled all his life to remember was therefore not a forgotten romance, as Judy first imagined, but a personal relic of Lincoln's compassion. Christian and Judy realize they have recovered both the historic object and the memory Colby had wanted preserved.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on February 7, 1945. It is listed as episode 324 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Helen Claire.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_9a91ea60f6bb704c0617.title: The Seeing Eye Pt2
paragraphs: Blind pianist Peg Foster, now moving independently with her Seeing Eye dog Mara, begins giving music lessons and hopes to earn a teaching position at the McCary Institute of Music. Founder Dan McCary blocks the appointment solely because Peg is blind and even threatens to withdraw his financial support if the institute hires her. By chance, however, McCary hears Peg play beautifully at a pupil's home without realizing who she is or that she cannot see. After learning the truth, he admits that his assumptions were wrong and reverses his opposition, clearing the way for Peg's appointment. The job proves to Peg that she can support herself rather than be a burden, but she still hesitates over whether a blind woman has the right to marry Joe Hardy. Dr. Christian tells her that love, character and the life she and Joe can build together matter more than her blindness. Peg accepts Joe's proposal, with Mara ready to be part of the wedding.

grh_9a127c08a4944c028a6e.title: No Time for Love
paragraphs: Sophisticated magazine photographer Katherine Grant is assigned to photograph the sandhogs building a tunnel under the river and immediately clashes with rough, self-confident worker Jim Ryan. After Ryan is injured protecting her during a construction accident, Kate hires him as a model and sets out to prove that his swagger, manners and physical appeal are completely incompatible with her cultured life and her relationship with wealthy Henry Fulton. Every attempt to make Ryan look ridiculous only makes Kate more attracted to him, while Ryan refuses to be reshaped into the kind of man she thinks she should want. When Kate finally stops treating her feelings as an experiment, she chooses Ryan openly, leaving Henry and her carefully designed ideas about romance behind.

grh_9ae8866ca3bfcd4d299c.title: Pacific Victory 1945
paragraphs: A dramatized adaptation of correspondent Joseph Driscoll's Pacific Victory 1945 surveys the American war against Japan and argues that victory depends on men, leadership, weapons and sustained support from the home front. It profiles commanders including MacArthur, Nimitz and Halsey, recalls the cost paid by wounded and dead servicemen, and rejects the idea of an easy shortcut to defeating Japan. The broadcast ends by urging civilians not to relax as the European war advances and to treat victory in the Pacific as an urgent national goal.
This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on October 3, 1944. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast.
